name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,337

clue.text: Agreement announced for transatlantic transport

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: concord is harmony or agreement

explanation.surface: A treaty is proclaimed about air travel across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: Concord and the supersonic airliner's name sound the same; only the final E differs on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Concorde was the supersonic passenger jet that flew between London, Paris and New York.

clue.text: Notice left in city for rising comedian

indicators.note: in places the first pair of words inside the next
in a down entry rising means read from bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
to see is to notice
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A poster in town announces an up-and-coming stand-up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, rising means the whole thing is read from the bottom up. The City of London is the financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cleese is the British comic actor of Monty Python and Fawlty Towers.

clue.text: Sister, one kept in business as messenger

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a nun is a religious sister
I is the Roman numeral one
Co. is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A sister and another person are held up at work running errands.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuncio is a papal envoy, the Pope's ambassador, and nuncio is Latin for messenger.

clue.text: Shade from loch recorded

indicators.note: from means taken out of the following words, so the answer lies within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A colour captured on film at a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: A loch is a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a yellowish-brown earth pigment and the colour named after it.

clue.text: Article about college penned by French painter, philosopher and novelist

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the next
penned means shut in a pen, so these letters are enclosed by the following word

blocks.note: Jacques-Louis David, the French neoclassical painter
John Stuart Mill, the English philosopher
the definite article
C is the abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: An essay on a college written by a French artist-thinker-writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Painter and philosopher both look like part of a list describing the novelist; only the last word defines, and the others supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: David Mitchell is the British author of Cloud Atlas and The Bone Clocks.

clue.text: Brush that's about right for untidy figure

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: to scuff is to brush or scrape against something
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A grooming brush is just the thing for someone who looks a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: SCUFF goes round R to make SCRUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruff is informal British slang for a scruffy, unkempt person.

clue.text: Artist embroidering tale in poetic form

indicators.note: embroidering a story means embellishing it, so the letters are worked into a new pattern
in places the reworked letters inside the next word

blocks.note: a canto is a section of a long poem
four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter dresses up a story in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Embroidering looks like something the artist does, but it works on the word tale alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaletto was the eighteenth-century Venetian painter famous for his views of Venice.

clue.text: Release top diplomat's identity badge

blocks.note: the UN, the United Nations, is the home of diplomats
a button is a round pin badge worn to show identity or allegiance

explanation.surface: A senior envoy's ID badge is handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: Top diplomat looks like a single phrase; top belongs to the definition, a shirt or blouse to be undone.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbutton a top is to undo its fastenings, releasing it.

clue.text: Line scrawled in note showing e.g. text on a storage device

definitions.text: e.g. text on a storage device

indicators.note: a scrawl is messy writing, so the letters come out jumbled
in puts the jumbled letters inside the next word

blocks.note: a person of note has fame
four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A line hastily written on a memo saved to disk.
explanation.walkthrough: Note looks like a scribbled message but means renown.
explanation.definitionFit: A filename is the identifying label of a stored file, and text is a typical example of one.

clue.text: Dine fancily, taken with hot site for cooking in Dutch city

indicators.note: doing something fancily means elaborately, with flourishes, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
an oven is where food is cooked

explanation.surface: Someone eating out in style, with hot food from the oven, somewhere in the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Eindhoven is a large city in the southern Netherlands, home of Philips and PSV.

clue.text: Go astern at sea to attract fish? It's of scant value

indicators.note: at sea means confused and tossed about, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: eight letters rearranged
hake is a sea fish, here plural

explanation.surface: A fishing boat reverses to lure a catch, which turns out worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: No great shakes is a British idiom meaning unremarkable or not very good.

clue.text: Number snubbed inventor - and another

indicators.note: snubbed puns on snub-nosed, cut short, so the word loses its end

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
Alexander Graham Bell, inventor of the telephone

explanation.surface: A mysterious figure gives one inventor the cold shoulder, and then a second.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: the snubbed inventor is the telephone's, and the answer is a second inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel invented dynamite before founding the prizes, so he is a second inventor.

clue.text: Minister's brass?

blocks.note: surface reading: a church's brass memorial plaque or candlesticks
setter's reading: brass is slang for money, so a clergyman's pay

explanation.walkthrough: Brass suggests church fittings, but it is British slang for cash; a minister is paid a fixed salary.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is the fixed regular salary paid to a clergyman, the classic term for a vicar's pay.

clue.text: Tasteless stuff shown by, say, retired Catholic

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, as does say
Latin as in the Latin (Roman Catholic) Church

explanation.surface: An elderly Catholic is shown displaying something bland.
explanation.walkthrough: Retired applies backwards to say, not to Catholic, as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatin is a colourless, tasteless protein substance used to set jellies.

clue.text: Noticed minor changes in investigators' facility

indicators.note: the phrase reads as minor changes, but changes tells us to alter the order of the letters

blocks.note: twelve letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spots small alterations at a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: An incident room is the office police set up to coordinate a major investigation.

clue.text: Criminal fellow restricted by tight pledges for repayment

indicators.note: restricted means hemmed in, so the letter is enclosed by the next word

blocks.note: near means stingy, tight with money
F is the abbreviation for fellow
an IOU is a written promise to repay a debt

explanation.surface: A crook is held back by mean people's promises to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Tight meaning stingy is everyday British usage, and near carries the same sense of tight-fisted.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefarious means wicked or criminal.

clue.text: A lot of fish served up in front of lake restaurant

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the word loses its last letter
in a down entry, served up means presented from bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: a perch is a freshwater fish
Lake Erie, one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A big fish dinner served at a lakeside eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: A creperie is a restaurant or café specialising in crêpes, thin French pancakes.

clue.text: Figure on board supporting Labour politician, sham opponent

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means placed underneath, so this piece comes second

blocks.note: Jack Straw, Labour Home and Foreign Secretary
a chess or draughts piece is a man

explanation.surface: A board member backs a Labour MP against a fake rival.
explanation.walkthrough: Figure on board sounds like a company director; it is a game piece. Labour is Britain's centre-left party.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw man is a misrepresented argument or feeble opponent set up to be easily knocked down.

clue.text: Indulgence that's not good getting approval

indicators.note: not good means without the letter standing for good, so it is removed

blocks.note: gratification is indulging a desire
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A moral warning that self-indulgence is bad, yet earns approval.
explanation.walkthrough: Not good sounds like a moral verdict; it removes G from the front of GRATIFICATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratification is formal approval or confirmation, as of a treaty.

clue.text: Companion in seat crumpled bag

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the following letters
something crumpled is crushed out of shape, so its letters lose their order

blocks.note: four letters rearranged
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A friend in the passenger seat squashes a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A sachet is a small sealed bag or packet, holding sugar, shampoo and the like.

clue.text: Rank Epstein's work, say, not close to Moore

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is wanted
not means without, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: Jacob Epstein was a sculptor, so sculptures; say marks an example
its final letter

explanation.surface: Ranking one sculptor's output against Henry Moore's.
explanation.walkthrough: Moore looks like the second sculptor, but only his last letter is used, removed from STATUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is standing or position in a hierarchy, which is what rank means.

clue.text: Plain promotional work that is following broadcast

indicators.note: following places one piece after another in the order of the answer

blocks.note: PR is public relations
to air a programme is to broadcast it
i.e. is Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A straightforward advertising campaign follows a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Plain looks like an adjective, but it is the noun for open flat land.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a large flat grassland, a kind of plain, especially in North America.

clue.text: Unusually hardy conservationists in main outlet

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon way, so the letters are put in an uncommon order

blocks.note: the five letters rearranged
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage and conservation charity

explanation.surface: Tough environmentalists turn up at an important outlet.
explanation.walkthrough: Main is the water main, not an adjective meaning chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydrant is a pipe fitting through which water can be drawn from a water main.

clue.text: Noted bowler getting duck

blocks.note: first meaning: Sir Francis ..., famously finishing his game of bowls before facing the Armada
second meaning: a male duck

explanation.surface: A famous cricket bowler is out for nought.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowler and duck suggest cricket, where a duck is a score of zero; the bowler here plays bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: Drake bowled on Plymouth Hoe in legend, and a drake is the male of the duck species.

clue.text: Sly feature in game clubs disowned

indicators.note: disowned means cast off, so the letter is dropped

blocks.note: crambo is an old rhyming word game
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards

explanation.surface: Someone cunning plays a game but disowns their golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Sly is Sylvester Stallone, not cunning. CRAMBO loses its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambo is the action film franchise starring Sylvester 'Sly' Stallone, so a feature film of his.

clue.text: Large Swedish company's fashionable instantly

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
IKEA, the Swedish furniture firm, with its possessive S
hot means in fashion

explanation.surface: A big Swedish firm's trendy goods appear at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a shot is an idiom meaning very quickly, at once, as fast as a fired bullet.

clue.text: Discussion of unduly solemn chap

indicators.note: discussion is talk, so the word is heard spoken rather than seen written

blocks.note: earnest means intensely serious

explanation.surface: A conversation about some over-serious man.
explanation.walkthrough: A nod to Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest, which turns on the same pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's first name, and crosswords use chap or man for any male name.

clue.text: A boss set in order insulating material

indicators.note: putting things in order means arranging them, so the letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A manager tidies up the lagging on site.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral once widely used for fire-resistant and thermal insulation.
